etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Usually considered a compound of 実(み) (mi, “fruit”) + 乗(の)る (noru, “to ride”). Alternatively, noru may be a corruption of なる (naru, “to become; to bear fruit”); compare the form 実(みな)る (minaru), attested in the Nihon Shoki.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the classical lower bigrade (下二段活用(しもにだん) (shimo nidan)) verb 流(なが)る (nagaru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First cited to the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE, and likely extant earlier as the intransitive verb 苦しむ (kurushimu, “to suffer, to be stressed out”) was first cited to the Kojiki of 712 CE.
Analyzable as a compound of bound morpheme ⟨kuru-⟩ (indicates stress or temper) + ⟨-si⟩ (adjectivizing suffix, gives object the possession of the adjective's quality), ultimately from Proto-Japonic *kuru. Compare 狂う (kuruu, “to be mad, to get angry”). Compare also Miyako 苦 (guri) against Miyako 悲す (kanasu, Japanese 悲しい (kanashii, “sad”)).
The modern form kurushii is derived from Early Middle Japanese adjective 苦(くる)し (kurushi), with the 終(しゅう)止(し)形(けい) (shūshikei, “predicative form”) ending in し (shi) first replaced with the 連(れん)体(たい)形(けい) (rentaikei, “attributive form”) ending in しき (shiki), and then with the medial /-k-/ falling out to result in an ending of しい (shii).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 褒む (pomu), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From classical 下二段 verb 解く (toku).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kupu/ → */kuwu/ → /kuu/
From Old Japanese. from Proto-Japonic *kup-.
The medial /w/ vanishes because Japanese does not have a /wu/ phoneme. It surfaces though in various conjugations, such as the negative form kuwanai or the passive form kuwareru.
Possibly cognate with 口(くち) (kuchi, “mouth”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally a compound of 根 (ne, “root”, more specifically signifying somewhere hidden away) + 住み (sumi, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 住む sumu, “to live in a place, to reside”), meaning roughly “one who lives in hidden places”. The sumi changes to zumi as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Abbreviation of nezumi. Used in some compounds.
